claim_boundary: All companies, people, objections, approvals, and comments in this file are fictional AI-simulated buyer personas.
This is not customer evidence, market demand, revenue, adoption, willingness-to-pay proof, or independent third-party validation.
The simulation is used to pressure-test procurement, security, finance, logistics, onboarding, and pilot-readiness materials.
A simulated APPROVE_PILOT decision does not authorize processing any real customer data.
This simulation is not independent of the builder.

profile.freight_profile: LTL + parcel heavy, centralized AP, existing freight-payment/audit provider
profile.main_problem: suspects incumbent audit misses accessorial and contract leakage

bots.rationale: Would fund a bounded second-look pilot because the attribution model avoids paying success fees on incumbent-known credits, but wants a blind customer benchmark and a clearly bounded commercial model before expansion.
questions: What percentage of candidate dollars survive human review and become realized recovery?
How do you prove a recovery was incremental rather than already in our incumbent workflow?
What is the buyer's downside if the population is clean?
conditions_to_approve: Use a no-upfront or tightly capped pilot structure.
Freeze incumbent output before RecoveryOS attribution.
Report realized recovery separately from candidate and validated dollars.

bots.rationale: The second-look positioning avoids replacing the incumbent system and can start with a bounded historical population. Human review is acceptable for the pilot.
questions: Which LTL and parcel charge families are supported today?
How long from data handoff to first reviewed findings?
Can the pilot avoid carrier contact until we approve specific findings?
conditions_to_approve: Start with LTL and parcel only.
Keep all carrier contact buyer-approved.
Provide evidence drill-down for every asserted dollar.

bots.rationale: Read-only historical review and explicit duplicate/pre-existing-credit suppression fit AP controls. Wants reconciliation outputs that can be tied back to invoice IDs.
questions: Can every finding map to invoice, shipment, authority and later credit?
How are automatic credits and open disputes excluded?
Can findings be exported for internal reconciliation?
conditions_to_approve: Read-only source access.
No posting or payment change without separate authorization.
Invoice-level reconciliation register.

bots.rationale: A small single-tenant pilot may be acceptable with minimal data and named access, but current lack of independent penetration-test evidence and provider backup/encryption evidence prevents broad production approval.
questions: Where exactly is customer data stored?
What provider encryption and backup evidence exists?
Can we use a buyer-controlled workspace for the first pilot?
conditions_to_approve: Buyer-controlled or separately approved single-tenant workspace.
Document current subprocessor/data-flow boundary.
No claim of SOC 2 or independent pen test.

profile.freight_profile: parcel + LTL + TL + intermodal across multiple business units
profile.main_problem: wants measurable independent audit assurance without disrupting existing TMS/AP stack

bots.rationale: The financial-truth model is attractive, but synthetic accuracy evidence is insufficient for enterprise budget approval. Wants a blind pilot with a pre-agreed false-positive ceiling and measured analyst effort.
questions: What is the independently adjudicated false-positive-dollar rate?
How many reviewer hours are required per 1,000 invoices?
What is actual realized recovery after reversals?
conditions_to_approve: Blind frozen population.
Buyer-owned truth adjudication.
Explicit false-positive-dollar ceiling and reviewer-hour reporting.

bots.rationale: Would not approve enterprise customer-data processing yet because MFA, enterprise SSO, independent penetration testing, SOC 2 Type II/ISO evidence, and provider backup/encryption attestations are not complete.
questions: Where is the independent penetration-test report?
Can we enforce SAML/OIDC SSO and MFA?
What is the tested RPO/RTO for the exact production database?
conditions_to_approve: MFA and enterprise SSO.
Independent penetration-test report with retest closure.
Provider encryption and backup/restore evidence.
Formal security-assurance package acceptable to enterprise procurement.

bots.rationale: Commercial wedge is understandable, but enterprise onboarding is incomplete without external security evidence, current DPA/subprocessor package, insurance/contract terms, and a referenceable customer outcome.
questions: Do you have SOC 2 Type II or equivalent?
What subprocessors receive customer content?
Can you provide a reference customer with realized recovery?
conditions_to_approve: Complete security questionnaire and DPA/subprocessor answers.
External assurance evidence.
At least one genuine referenceable customer result or approved blind proof.

bots.rationale: Likes the second-look concept but needs repeatable ERP/TMS integration and multi-business-unit onboarding. Global currency/operational support is not mature enough for enterprise-wide rollout.
questions: Which SAP/Oracle/TMS connectors are production ready?
How is business-unit isolation enforced?
Can results reconcile across multiple currencies and regions?
conditions_to_approve: Pilot one U.S. business unit first.
Prove one named ERP/TMS integration path.
Defer global rollout until currency/regional operations are supported.

profile.freight_profile: multi-client LTL/FTL/parcel audit and managed transportation
profile.main_problem: wants a second-look engine to challenge its own audit process without exposing one client to another

bots.rationale: RecoveryOS could be valuable as an internal challenger layer, but a 3PL needs repeatable client onboarding, strict isolation, and higher-scale concurrency evidence before embedding it in operations.
questions: Can one client ever see another client's data?
How many concurrent client populations can be processed?
Can we automate handoff from our TMS without bespoke work?
conditions_to_approve: Pilot with one client and isolated tenant.
Prove named TMS ingestion.
Run multi-tenant concurrency test before broader rollout.

bots.rationale: Architecture is promising but not ready for platform embedding without enterprise SSO/MFA, named integrations, higher-scale HTTP/concurrency evidence, and documented operational SLOs.
questions: What are the API rate limits and availability SLOs?
Can we federate identity and automate provisioning?
Where are the load-test results for concurrent tenants?
conditions_to_approve: Enterprise SSO/MFA.
Published API/SLO contract.
Concurrent multi-tenant load evidence.
Production TMS connector.

bots.rationale: The incumbent-challenge engine is directly aligned with a 3PL audit QA function. Explicit suppression of existing findings and duplicates makes a one-client shadow audit useful immediately.
questions: Can the system ingest our existing audit result as the frozen incumbent source?
Can reviewers see why a case was marked challenger-only?
Can we measure miss rate without changing our live payment flow?
conditions_to_approve: Shadow mode only.
No external carrier action.
Freeze existing audit output before challenge.

bots.rationale: Evidence lineage is attractive, but enterprise accounting needs cost-center/GL allocation and a clear reconciliation path to the actual payment/credit system.
questions: How do findings map to client GL and cost centers?
How are carrier credits reconciled to our actual payment system?
Can reversals be posted back into the recovery report automatically?
conditions_to_approve: Provide GL/cost-center export or connector.
Integrate payment/credit reconciliation with an actual provider.
Keep reversals visible in net realized recovery.
